sections.body: We hold a book the right way up. 📖 We start at the front cover.
We read words from left to right ➡️, and turn pages one at a time.
After a story, we can tell it again: what happened first, next and at the end?
Stories teach us new words. Try using a new word today!
Read together daily. Ask 'What happened next?' and 'How did they feel?'. Let your child turn the pages and point to words as you read.

quiz.q: Which way do we read words in English?
hints: Think about how your finger moves when you point at words.
Open a book. Is the first word of each line on the left side or the right side?
When we count blocks in a row, we start at one side and go across. Reading English starts on the left.
quiz.explain: In English, we read from left to right ➡️.

quiz.q: In 'The Three Little Pigs', what does the wolf try to do to the houses?
hints: Think about the wolf's big breath.
'I'll huff and I'll puff and I'll…'
In 'Goldilocks', she tries the porridge. In 'The Three Little Pigs', the wolf tries to ___ the houses down.
quiz.explain: The wolf huffs and puffs to blow the houses down! 💨
